text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Minor earthquake measuring 3.6 on the Richter scale hit Sarajevo Thursday afternoon causing minimal material damage.
- Russian gas company Gasexport will reduce gas supplies to Bosnia on February 24 due to a $12.3 million debt, it said in a statement sent to the Bosnian gas import company Energoinvest.
- Bosnia's Council of Ministers failed to adopt a "quick start package" of economic reform laws.
- The Moslem-Croat federation's Sarajevo canton is to set up a police force on February 26, it was announced after federation forum meeting in the U.S. embassy in Sarajevo.

- Some 120 Bosnian Croats will be prevented from travelling to some European and overseas countries after being allegedly charged with criminal acts and violation of human rights during a recent incident in the divided southern town of Mostar, unofficial sources in Brussels say.
- Those responsible for recent incidents in Mostar must be condemned, Elisabeth Rehn, United Nations Rapporteur for Human Rights, said during her visit to Mostar on Thursday.

- Haris Silajdzic, co-chairman of Bosnia's Council of Ministers, urges adoption of laws on ownership, privatisation and restitution and their integration into laws on economic reform, saying this is a condition for realisation of projects defined by the Dayton peace accords.

- Defence lawyers for seven Bosnian Moslems, who were arrested and charged with multiple murders by Bosnian Serb police last year, requested postponement of their hearing. The accused Bosnian Moslems known as the Zvornik Seven are still detained in Bijeljina prison in the Serb Republic.

- The leading Moslem party SDA prepares for the upcoming local elections scheduled for June this year and opposes their holding in the Bosnian southern town of Mostar and the disputed town of Brcko since there are no conditions for their realisation, Halid Genjac, spokesman of the leading Moslem party SDA says at party press conference in Sarajevo.
- A United Nations spokesman in Sarajevo said the report on the last incidents in Mostar when one Bosnian Moslem was killed and 22 others injured has not been completed yet.

- The International Committee of the Red Cross is concerned about a gas cut off and says it might leave thousands of elderly people without their daily meal. The ICRC and German Red Cross run 16 public kitchens which feed more than 10,000 old people in the Sarajevo area.

- The Islamic Republic of Iran is likely to provide funds for the construction of a bridge over the river Sava near Orasje which will link Bosnia and Croatia, secretary to the Iranian embassy in Zagreb told Bosnian state-run news agency BH PRESS.
